But at the time, when you were in Grude and when you were working alongside Mr. Boban and you were involved in financial matters, did you then have any knowledge or indication that there was some form of official funding on the part of the Republic of Croatia or not? This, of course would mean that the money would have been provided or funded by the budget of the state.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, yesterday or the day before yesterday when we were speaking, I said to you that this was 1992 and 1993. Believe me, I wouldn't know where the money came from. Since what happened to me happened, I said that from the Republic of Croatia in 1992 about 1.4 million German marks came, but not from the budget but from the Republic of Croatia, from the money that was paid by our people from abroad; and, in 1993, it was about 4.5 million.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Do I understand -- excuse me. Do I understand, Your Honour, that, Mr. Rupcic has now become an expert witness, who has conducted an analysis of all the budgets of the Republic of Croatia? Excuse me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He is your witness and --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, and I asked him about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- he answered the question yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes. I asked him about specific questions about specific documents and specific transactions: Did you withdraw this cash on this day? Did you go and pick up this money? Is that your signature? Those are the questions. I didn't make him into an expert on the financial dealings of the Republic of Croatia. This is not proper, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Just for the record, on line 10 on page 46, Your Honour, it says "ABiH," and I believe you intended or you'd said "HVO." So that should be corrected, so not ABiH. That's all. I have no further questions, Mr. President. I do apologise for, you know, all this storm in this little teapot of ours. The intention was merely to elicit the kind of testimony that the Prosecution was attempting to elicit, and, unfortunately, the Prosecutor is not happy with his own witness. I cannot help that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is now time to have a break. We shall have a 20-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Nozica, according to the calculations of the registrar, you should have one hour and-- according to the very accurate calculations of the registrar, you should have one hour and 45 minutes: An hour for you, half an hour from Mr. Pusic, and 15 minutes from Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon. Thank you, Your Honours. Thank you, Your Honour. Yes, that would be the right time frame.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Good day, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now I would like to deal with some of the things you explained during your direct examination; namely, when you explained how the defence department in 1992 and in part of 1993 or throughout 1993 paid personal incomes to professional and active-duty units. I would like you to confirm whether I understood correctly what it was that you were saying. Members of the professional units signed professional contracts, and that was the reason why all members of these units had salaries paid to them. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Before we proceed, since you and I speak the same language, please keep your headphones on. For the interpretation, we need to pause between my question and your answer so that everything could be interpreted. As for the active-duty members, do you agree that these are members of the commands of the Main Staff of the HVO, the operative zones, the operative groups, and the commands of brigades? Would that be it, the active-duty members who were paid by the defence department?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be it. Brigades and units have a set establishment of active-duty personnel.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You explained that in the right way. Through this book, logbook, it is exactly established a which personnel is in these positions, and these persons were paid out these salaries; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Yesterday, on several occasions, we heard from you during your direct examination yesterday and the day before yesterday and today during cross-examination by Mr. Karnavas, and we saw this through certain documentation, that some municipalities also financed some units. Now I would just like to ask you to go back to a document. You don't have to look at it. You don't have to go through Mr. Karnavas's binder. It's going to be in e-court, because I'd just like to clarify one thing. That is 1D 01762. While we're waiting for the document in e-court, I'm going to remind you what this is about. This is a document that was adopted by the HVO of the municipality of Livno on the 24th of September, 1993. That is a decision on the professionalisation of the army within brigade, the HVO Brigade Petar Kresimir IV, and defining adequate salaries of TIP. Sir, you answered that professional units, especially you said this in response to the intervention made by His Honour Judge Antonetti, were supposed to be paid by the defence department. However, this decision dates back to September 1993. We see in paragraph II, let's have a look at it together, it says that it is the HVO of Livno, the municipality of Livno, made a decision that members of the professional units of that brigade, starting from the 1st of September, 1993, these members would receive a special salary adequate to TIP, something that is called "TIP." You said that you did not see this document before. You said that there was great diversity in payments. You said that there was not an established system, and you also said that the defence department -- or rather, your financial department did not always have enough resources to pay out salaries and to cover other expenses, even for those brigades and units for which they had the duty to do so. Doesn't this document show that at least from the 24th of September, 1993, the municipality of Livno took over the obligation to pay these professional units, too, within the brigade of Petar Kresimir IV?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what can be seen in this document; however, I have to note, and we saw this in previous documents, while they were Home Guard Units, they were still paying their salaries.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I have a problem in terms of understanding here. Are you sure that this was a Home Guard Unit, or was this a mobilised brigade?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A mobilised brigade means a Home Guard Brigade. It's the same thing. Before, in the Yugoslav People's Army, within that system, you had the Territorial Defence, and the Croatian expression for Territorial Defence is Home Guard regiments or Home Guard Units.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: On the basis of what I've learned so far in this case, I didn't think I would be dealing with this, but there were mobilised members who were in brigades - just a moment, let me finish - then there were separate Home Guard Brigades. Am I right? If you don't know anything about this, if you think it's the same, I'm not going to insist on it.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It's the same brigades. Mobilised brigades are Home Guard Brigades. These are people who did a certain type of work; and then, because of the war and in order to defend their homes, they were mobilised in a unit that was a Home Guard Unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: That is your interpretation. I'm not going to go into that any further, but please let us --

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Somebody's intervening. Right? I think that Mr. Praljak would like to help me, and I'm not opposed to that, because I'm almost certain that as far as this particular subject matter is concerned he knows more than I do.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel please speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Rupcic, there were professional brigades, there were brigades attached to municipalities, and -- and there were reserve brigades. Now, it was only later that those brigades were -- came to be known as Domobrani or Home Guard brigades. Before that, they were reserve brigades; and then, later on, they had Home Guards who were over the age of 55 or 60, and these people were referred to as Domobrani. But professional brigades, reserve brigades that changed their composition by a third, a half, or two-thirds would be at home while a third would be up at the battle front, and Domobrani, the Home Guards, would be only those who were mobilised from these brigades to perform some very light duties. So would you agree with my interpretation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You have far greater experience in that area than I do. I would stick to my profession, which means finances. I allow for the possibility that that is so.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to thank Mr. Praljak. I'd like to continue. I'd like to inform the Trial Chamber that, during the preparations for cross-examination of this witness, Mr. Prlic's Defence cooperated with the Stojic Defence. However, we weren't able to cover all the documents, all of us together. So I'd just like to follow on from what Mr. Karnavas was doing.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And, in that sense would, you take a look at my own document which is 2D 00538. It is the pink binder that you have in front of you, and it is the seventh the document from the top, the seventh document in order. Tell me when you've found.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've found it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: This is, in fact, a decision on the financing of the Croatian Defence Council of Livno municipality - so we're still staying with Livno municipality - by our workers temporarily employed abroad. Now, Mr. Rupcic, in my next few questions, I'm going to try to show documents and establish that the municipalities, regardless of their obligation of the defence department, financed and collected certain money to finance the brigades which were in their area. Now, Mr. Karnavas showed you document 1D 01761. You don't have to look for it. I'm just saying this for the transcript. The date is the 26th of March, 1993; then another document, 1D 00307, dated the 2nd of April, 1993, from Livno municipality about this kind of financing. I want to show you the document because it is a document dated the 9th of December, 1992; that is to say, from this document, which is very similar to the one we've already seen, it follows that already in 1992 the Livno municipality had taken a decision on financing the defence. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I'd now like to ask you to look at Article III of that document, and you've spoken at length about the situation. This is what it says: "All funds gathered abroad for financing the OHVO of Livno municipality shall be directly to the Livno community in Frankfurt,"" And then there's a bank account number. Article IV addresses that matter, too. Is that what you said, that all the funds that were paid in for the defence of the HVO in 1992 and in 1993 - and that was Mr. Praljak's intervention, too - was in fact paid in to certain accounts outside Bosnia-Herzegovina and indeed outside Croatia, and that's what this document says? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Correct. So we see here that this municipality of Livno had opened an account in Frankfurt. I didn't know about that account.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you. Now let's take a look at the next document. It is 2D 00536. It is the fifth document from the top in my binder. We're going to go through this document quickly, and it is the wartime council for Posusje municipality. Tell me when you've found it. It is the war defence council of Posusje, and it is dated the 4th of June, 1992. Once again, it is a decision about remuneration to mobilised recruits, and that's what we mentioned a moment ago --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Mobilised conscripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, in Article III, let's see what it says: "Mobilise military conscripts who did not receive compensation at their companies, institutions, or at privately owned businesses due to any reason, as well as mobilised military conscripts who are not employed, shall receive monetary compensation from the fund for the defence of Posusje municipality." Article IV goes on to say: "Mobilised military conscripts can receive monetary compensation own on one basis. That is either at the company, institution, and privately owned business or from the fund for the defence of Posusje municipality." Now, in the statement of reasons on the second page of this document, it explains why this decision is being made, and it says: "War events have had deep consequences and have deeply affected the overall life of our municipality. The economy is on its knees." And then, in Article VII: "for mobilised military recruits, that shall be 6.000 Croatian dinars." Now, we see from this decision by the war council of Posusje municipality that, in June, the municipality of Posusje has made a decision to finance mobilised military conscripts; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I'm now going to go on -- to move on, but I have a question before that. When you distributed personal income, salaries, at that time, did you know that the municipalities themselves in their own way were assisting units that had been established or that were on their territory?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I'd like to move on to the Tomislav municipality, and for that please look at document 2D 00539. It is the fourth document from the bottom of my binder. I have quite a number of documents but I have selected just the most characteristic ones which refer to what you spoke about during your examination-in-chief. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: This is a decision by the Tomislav municipality dated the 21st of December, 1992, and it is in fact a conclusion made on amendments to the conclusion on taking measures against military conscripts who did not fulfil their obligations from the 15th of December, 1992. I'd like you now to take a look at point 3, paragraph 3, and then I'll ask you a question. It says: "The amount paid as an aid to the Republic of Croatia shall not be calculated into the settlement of financial obligations." Now, Mr. Rupcic, did you know, were you aware that Croatian citizens, and not only citizens who were Croats during the aggression, during the JNA attack against Croatia, paid in certain donations for assistance to Croatia in defending itself from the Serb aggression, and that all this was going on in 1991 and 1990; that is to say, far before the conflicts in Bosnia-Herzegovina began?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if you remember what I said, that is what I confirmed in my previous statements.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So from this decision made by the Tomislavgrad municipality, well, it states that you have certain obligations to finance units which were established in Tomislavgrad municipality, but it says that the amount paid as aid to the Republic of Croatia shall not be calculated into the settlement of these financial obligations. So Mijo Tokic says, the president of the HVO, you have a new obligation to assist the defence of the HVO; right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry. A while ago you referred to this, but we don't have your statements and that's a problem. And, in paragraph 3, there's something new, a new piece of information which I've just discovered. It seems that, as far as the municipalities are concerned, some funds were sent to the Republic of Croatia to help the Republic of Croatia. Is that how we should understand this paragraph, paragraph 3?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Judge, when I was talking about the overall aid which came in from the Republic of Croatia, I said at the time that the Croatian people from Bosnia-Herzegovina paid in considerable financial resources into the account in Villach, which was called the account for the defence of Croatia and Bosnia-Herzegovina. From that money paid into that account and other accounts, Bosnia-Herzegovina, or rather, the HVO received 1.400.000 in 1992 and 4.5 million in 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But my question was a more accurate question. I wanted to know whether this document establishes that there were funds that were -- the money was coming from these municipalities and sent to the Republic of Croatia and that the money was only coming from Croatian citizens abroad.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Croats who were living abroad. Now, the municipality would say, "Yes, you did pay in that money into that account, but it is your duty to defend your municipality, or, rather, to financing your own municipality. So the fact that you paid in money over there, we're not interested in that. We don't count that. Give some money to us."

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: For us to clarify this whole issue and the question raised by Judge Antonetti, well, you have given an answer and you said that it wasn't the municipalities which financed the Croatian defence but individuals. Now, I'd like to ask you, to make certain that what you're saying is correct, for us to go back to a document shown to you by Mr. Karnavas, which is in my own binder, and it is 2D 00540. It will come up on e-court but you can also look at did in hard copy. It is the third document from the bottom. Tell me when you've found it. It's come up on e-court. We'll see from that document that, in fact, the Tomislavgrad municipality, on the 2nd of August, 1992, made this decision to finance the requirements of a total national defence; and pursuant to this, in Article 2, it gives -- passes this responsibility to citizens. It has so much for men, so much for women, and then citizens employed in Austria, and then you have the men, women columns. Was this in fact financing by individuals and not financing of the municipality, which possibly the municipality then transferred to Croatia?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's what I said. The municipality collected money from individuals, and it didn't send that money to Croatia. It financed its own soldiers on its own territory.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Before that, it was individuals from that municipality as individuals paying in sums of money for -- in order to assist the defence of Croatia from the JNA aggression; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I said a moment ago. They said, "What you paid into those accounts, we're not interested in any way of that. You should now pay in to the municipality money that can be distributed to their own soldiers." So it was the defence department that did not have information and did not dispose of the money that was paid into the municipalities.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers kindly slow down and make pauses between question and answer. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've been asked to slow down. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you now to move on to another document. It is 2D 00535, which is the fourth document in my binder. Tell me when you've found it, please.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have found it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: This is a document compiled by the Croatian Defence Council of Tomislavgrad, on the 20th of February, 2003 [as interpreted]. It is the financing of Tomislavgrad --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: -- until the present day. It calls for financing to be taken over and to compensate the costs incurred to date. Now, in the first sentence, and I'm just going to focus on certain parts of the text, it says in the first sentence: "As you already know..." This was sent to the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna, the Croatian Defence Council. It says: "As you already know, Tomislavgrad municipality and its area ... has 3.500 soldiers engaged, of which 2.800 soldiers from its territory." It says: "From the beginning of the war until the present time, Tomislavgrad municipality did not receive financial help either from the HZ HB or any other municipality. It had to bear all war expenses by itself, and thus was forced to engage its material and monetary funds." Now, take a look at the Croatian version and the last paragraph on the first page. It says: "Within the Kralj Tomislav Brigade, there is one battalion from Kupres, one battalion from Posusje. It could hardly be expected from Kupres municipality for it to bear the expenses for its army and refugees by itself, and also Posusje municipality did not take over expenses for its battalion ..." Well, it's a battalion that was in the Tomislavgrad area. I don't know if you know anything about that, but that's what it says here. And then it goes on to say in the Croatian text: "Besides that, the organisation and training of the Jajce battalion was organised, which after the fall of Jajce was again situated in the area of Tomislavgrad, together with the refugees, was borne by the Tomislavgrad municipality, which created additional financial and material burden." Now, we have a calculation of how much Tomislavgrad municipality spent on defence; and then, in continuation, there's a proposal asking that the HZ HB take over the financing of all expenses for defence and that it should compensate Tomislavgrad municipality for expenses incurred. Now, do you know that even after this date, the 20th of February, 1992 [as interpreted], in fact, this financing was continued by the Tomislavgrad municipality, or rather, the defence department never had sufficient funds for -- in order to finance all the members of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now I'd like to move on to another topic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My colleague tells me that that is mistake in the transcript, and I thank her for that. The page is 60, line 22. It's not 1992. That's right. It is 1993. That's the year.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: We're going to move on to another topic now, one that the Prosecutor insisted upon during the direct examination; namely, how decisions were made on the allocation of resources that were coming to your financial department. Who made these decisions in different periods of time? Could we now please focus on the initial period? We can say that that was 1992, and perhaps 1993, half of 1993, when you said, actually, that throughout that time, and even after that, there was never enough money; and that, to the best of your knowledge, the priorities were set by Mr. Boban as to who would be paid out. Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you did understand me correctly.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I assume that you still have the Prosecutor's binder in front of you. Yesterday, the Prosecutor showed you document number -- do you still have it?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Could you please take it. Yesterday, the Prosecutor showed you P 10290. We have the document in e-court, but could you please find it as well. It's going to be easier for you to see it.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've found it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: This is a payroll for the month of October 1992. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Before speaking to the Prosecutor, did you see this document?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before speaking to the Prosecutor, no, I do not recall.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You said that the document was not signed by Mr. Stojic, and that can be seen from the document itself.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You said that the document was signed by Mr. Majic, your superior. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I said that having seen the card of depositor signatures, I recognised the signature of Mr. Majic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: As we can see, the document is not verified by a stamp of the head of the defence department. Do you perhaps know what this stamp looked like?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Very well. Let us look at page 1. Was this document written on the official paper of the defence department? Did you have occasion to see that? It's the upper part.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It said the defence department on the top.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: On the document, there is a log number, whatever you call it, 03-2541/92; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Could you please have a look at the document -- or rather, document P 00586. That is the document with a yellow sticker towards the bottom of my binder. Sir, when you find it, 586 is the number, yellow sticker.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've found it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: We are not going to go any further. Just look at page 1. It has to do with the establishment of the defence section, and it is a document dated the 17th of October, 1992, so just a day before the one that we looked at a minute ago. The number on it is 03-142. On this document, it says exactly what you said that the letterhead says, "the defence department"; right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Stojic signed that, and that cannot be contested; right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recognised it also from the card.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Let's go back to document P 0290?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Can counsel please speak into the microphone. We have great difficulty hearing her. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: We see a difference here in terms of the number of this document in addition to other noted differences, which makes it obvious that the document was not written at the office of the head of the defence department. Could you draw the same conclusion?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know where it was written, the form, that is, but I know, or rather, I see -- well, I have seen this difference, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Sir, I asked you all of this because you said that at first, when the HZ HB started functioning, as far as the allocation of resources was concerned, when there was money, Mr. Boban made the decisions. However, you also said and this document does show that this money was withdrawn and distributed to the mentioned units, and that cannot be contested; right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No doubt about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Sir, was there a technical problem? Well, I'm going to give you an assumption. Mr. Boban perhaps did not propose this document, did not give a number, did not give it to Mr. Majic to sign it. Would it be technically logical that it was drafted by -- that had it been drafted by Mr. Stojic, he could have done that in his office and sent it by fax to Grude; then it would have had the stamp, the signature, and the number that is required and that would show that this had to do with the things that he was deciding about at the time?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it would have been possible for them to do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I am sorry. I will slow down. The situation is identical with document P 0291. Can you find that document? Now it is that binder of documents, the Prosecution binder. Can you find the document that is the payroll actually?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I found it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: We haven't got it in e-court, but I hope that we will see it on e-court as well. The page is 0289 -- 0289-8284. That's the ERN number of the Croatian translation. So it's the same document, and the date is the same; however, these are just salaries for December; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You were authorised to collect the money by Mr. Jelavic and Mr. Majic?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You withdrew the money on the 17th of December 1992?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I would like to ask you to have a look at this document and see for which purposes this amount of money was withdrawn. Can you confirm that there's a reference here to the HVO in municipalities that were not within the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna? I'm going to help you. It is the HVO Zepce under number 1; then 2, Maglaj; 3, Novi Seher; 4, Teslic; 5, Zavidovici; and 12, Zenica. Am I right? To the best of your recollection, were these municipalities within the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, they were not.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Sir, do you know that the HVO -- that actually HVO units existed throughout the territory outside HZ HB, and that in some territories they even fought together with the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina against the Serb aggression?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I would like to note that these HVOs are noted in the previous list of salaries for October. The Prosecutor asked you, during your interview in 2005, why item 22 for the 1st Herzegovinian Brigade exceeds the amount for other cases. If you remember your answer, could you tell us what it was? It is 22.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This brigade was in the area of Capljina and Stolac; that is to say, that it included that area which was engaged in immediate activity. So, in that area, there was absolutely no economic activity. Nothing was functioning at the time. No money could be collected, so, well, almost half of that brigade consisted of Bosniaks.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Sir, was it a big brigade in terms of personnel levels?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It had about 5.000 men.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: As far as I remember, that's what you said to the Prosecutor, too. Did that brigade include Neum, Capljina, and Stolac, as far as you can remember?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that entire area.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Could you now find in my binder document 2D 00150. There is a yellow sticker there.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've found it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Sir, we see, in this document, it's a defence department document, the 9th of June, 1993. It says: "Overview of the national structure of the members of the HVO," and then it is being delivered. Please look at page 2, and we will find this 1st Herzegovinian brigade. It is under number 14 here. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: On the date, this was received in June 1993. In the month of June, can you confirm, if you remember, that already then there was a conflict between the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the HVO?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in certain areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am sorry. I apologise to interpreters. We are going to be more careful.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: At that point, the brigade has 4.686 members, out of which 1.659 are Muslims. That is roughly what you remember, too; right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: His Honour Judge Antonetti asked you about the professional unit called the Convicts Battalion, so could we have a look at item 36. It's the Convicts Battalion. It had 280 members, is that right, that is what it stated here, out of which 116 were Bosniaks or Muslims? Do you remember that it had a large number of Muslims?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall the exact number, but I did know that they had them.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Finally, sir, I would like to ask you to look at another document. If it's hard for you to find it I'm going to ask for it in e-court. It has to do with the transfer of resources and what you were involved in. P 10291 is an order issued by Mr. Susak. The document has an ERN number, 0289 -- 0289-8283. You'll see it on e-court.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, precisely. Thank you. Thank you. We are getting very efficient assistance.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Please, the Prosecutor showed you this document, but let us focus on this transaction of 306.000.000, et cetera, Croatian dinars. Does it say here, in paragraph 1, that this is a loan?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could counsel speak into the microphone. We really cannot hear her.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: We're going to move on to the annual report, so could you please look at the Prosecution binder. P 089 -- 08181 is the number, P 08181.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: When you find it, could you tell me.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please go to the page that has to do with the finance department and the page that has to do with the structure of revenue from the 1st of January until the 31st of December, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: It is roughly page 7.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You've found it, but the others need to follow it, too.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's not in my binder, so I will say in the Croatian version it is page 03469322. I'm sure that it will be found. I think that it's the seventh page in English, and I'm sure that the Honourable Trial Chamber will manage to find it as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: The Prosecutor asked you something about expenditures but not about revenues. Before any question about this balance sheet, Mr. Rupcic, can you confirm to us that the records of expenditures and revenues that were compiled in 1993 were proper and regular, and that can be seen from the cards that follow? Was everything recorded, all the expenditures and all the revenues in that year?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can confirm that absolutely everything was recorded and that this report went to the finance department, later the Ministry of Finance, the civilian one, and it was used as proof.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: We are talking about the structure of revenues here for all of 1993 expressed in Croatian dinars; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Let us try to see what it was in 1993 that the defence department of the HZ HB received from Croatia. I'm going to put a question to you, and you're going to tell me. Here it says, "Revenue from the budget and from donations." Is the first item the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Croatia, Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says, "The Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Croatia, Zagreb," but we're going back to my testimony earlier on, to the effect that the Republic of Croatia, or rather, the individuals such as Mr. Susak and Mr. Zagorac, were authorised to use money in foreign banks, deposited in foreign banks. So they were the signatories on the accounts. Their signatures were deposited, and they transferred the money.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: We'll come to that in due course, sir, but this is what it says here, and that was where we had our discussion when Mr. Karnavas asked you about this. You claim that large sums of money, donations from citizens of both Bosnia-Herzegovina and Croatia, were paid in to certain accounts for the defence of the HZ HB, and that part of that money, de facto, would appear as if it had passed through the Ministry of Defence of Croatia on a piece of paper like that. Am I right in saying that?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: But we're not going to deal with that now. We're just going to calculate the sum. You said the amount, and you told us how much there was in 1993 that came from Croatia. Here, we have the exact figures from a document provided to us by the Prosecution, so we don't have to guess. We can calculate it exactly, and please help us out here.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is 16.760.000 -- I beg your pardon, 16.764.924.236 Croatian dinars, which corresponds to --

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. We'll calculate it in just a moment. Would you take a look at the first item, where it says "Received in DEM." Does the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Croatia appear here as well?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: From the entire structure of revenues, these were only two items which arrived - and you can confirm that, can you not - from the Defence Ministry of the Republic of Croatia, or rather, that would be the sum total of all the individual transactions shown to you by the Prosecutor. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, do you believe me when I say - I'm not as good a mathematician as you are but I use the computer - that if you add up these two figures, it would come to 17.033.694.236 Croatian dinars?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I'm sure you can see that visually and check out the maths of that.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And you said that was about 4.5 million, if I understood you correctly, roughly 4.5 million; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Marks, marks? 4.5 million marks; right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Sir, to avoid any guesswork, the Prosecutor showed you many documents from which, with your help, we can calculate exactly what the exchange rate of the Croatian dinar was on different days. Since this is the sheaf for 1993 as a whole, I would like to ask you -- and this will come up on e-court, I assume, because we haven't had this document in e-court. But, anyway, it is in the binder which in the binder is P 10297, and the ERN number is 0342-4345.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As that contains a large number of documents, I would like to have it on e-court. The next one. That's not the right document. I'm looking at another document, ERN number 0342-4345. It is a document from the Privredna Banka of Zagreb, where it says "Sales" at the top.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I'd like to come back to a document, the document which shows the balance between expenditure and revenue, which is document 2118. 2118, Revenue. I can see "Republic of Croatia, Ministry of Defence, Zagreb," and I can a total of 16.764.924.236 Croatian dinars. Apparently, that would be a contribution from the Republic of Croatia. Next, on the next page, you can see the total of all the revenue. As a total, you have 185.682.783.197 dinars. This takes different items into account among which some foreign currency amounts; and, incidentally, I note that the HVO has a dollar amount for 1.156.000.997 dollars, et cetera. I think aren't dollars, because the Americans aren't in Tuzla. This is my reasoning. If I look at what Croatian Republic has given, 110.000.000.000 and 185.000.000.000, the direct funding from Croatia is less than 10 per cent. Correct me if I'm wrong.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, no, you're not wrong, but let me underline, once again. It's not that the Republic of Croatia gave that. It just transferred the money on. It went via Croatia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Fine.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I was going to come to that through my questions, but I just want to see if we can confirm what the witness said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could it be quick, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like us to arrive at the witness's answer - and he repeated his answer several times - at how much that sum was in marks, to confirm that through the documents that we have. We now have on e-court a document which is called "Sale." And in that document, we have all the elements on the basis of which we're able to calculate the exchange rate of the Croatian dinars for the 12th of November, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: We can see here - now, Witness, please help me out here - that 12.447.600 Croatian dinars is equal to 3.280 German marks. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: If we divide these two figures, then we would obtain the exchange rate, or rather, the value of one mark. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: When we calculate this division, it appears that 1 mark was equal to 3.795 Croatian dinars on the 21st of November, 1993, when this transaction was carried out?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So, following on from that calculation, although it cannot be applied for the 31st of December when the inflation was even greater; am I right in saying that?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Then, this sum, which came from Croatia, in fact would represent 4.488.445 German marks. Is that what you knew and what you testified about? Am I right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to move on now to another set of questions directly related to your last answer to His Honour Judge Antonetti, and it refers to donations. If I might interpret it in my own way, you in fact said you consider that the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Croatia sent on money from the resources collected and deposited in different accounts paid in by citizens, both of Croatia and Bosnia-Herzegovina, for assistance to Bosnia-Herzegovina. Am I right in saying that?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, I am going to continue on from where Mr. Karnavas left off in his cross-examination because I have several documents here, and one of the documents is technically perhaps better than the one shown by Mr. Karnavas. So let's look at 2D 00534, please, and it is the last document in my binder. It's the last document. It's a document described by -- or rather, signed by Mr. Boban on the 20th of April, and addressed to three people: Pero Milolaza, Martin Soljic, and Ivo Zrno. It is 1992. Let's see what Mr. Boban tells them: "Based on an invitation to all donors for a fund to aid for Herceg-Bosnia from abroad, please submit the cash which you brought to the Ministry of Finance of the Republic of Croatia. On the money order, state that payment is aid for Herceg-Bosna," and then it goes on to say, "please convey our deep gratitude to all the donors," et cetera, et cetera. I'm quite sure, sir, that you've never seen this document before. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. I've haven't seen, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You said that you knew that these funds existed; right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Especially after the affairs in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: From this document, does it emerge quite clearly that Mr. Boban is telling the donors that he asks that the cash that they brought in be hand over to the Ministry of Finance of the Republic of Croatia; and from this document, what you have been claiming all along can be seen that those donations were handed over to the Ministry of Finance of the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether to the Ministry of Finance or not, I didn't know that. But to accounts opened by the Croatian state in foreign banks, I knew about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Yes. It is my suggestion that not only the Ministry, yes, because we can see that, that is correct, and the funds that you showed in the balance sheet for 1993, that certain funds came from other accounts, not only via the Defence Ministry; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Let's look at another document that follows on from this is 2D 00533. It is the penultimate document in my binder, to see where the funds arrived ultimately and whether what Mr. Boban signed for here is correct. It is a confirmation from the Ministry of Finance, confirming the receipt of money, and that foreign currency was handed over to the tune 224.000 marks. It says: "The Ministry commits to inform the Croatian national committee at Grude about the amount of funds received which are allocated for the defence of Herceg-Bosna," and it says: "The Croatian Defence Council should inform municipalities in the communities of Herceg-Bosna." Their municipalities are enumerated. In the signatures -- and the signatures we have Martin Soljic, Pero Milolaza, and Ivo Zrno. They appeared in the first letter we mentioned signed by Mr. Boban; right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No verbal response].

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: From these two documents, I know you don't know about these two documents; but as you have already told us, you do know about how the system functioned; if not then, at least later on. So from this documents, can we see that those donor resources, quite a large number 224.000 deutschemarks, were money received from individuals handed over to the Ministry of Finance of the Republic of Croatia? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Sir, can we now take a look, once again, at a document that we've already seen? It's important in view of Judge Antonetti's question. It is 2D 00532, and it is the third document from the top. It is Mr. Boban's letter. We weren't able to see his actual signature a moment ago. Tell me when you've found it.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've found it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: It is true, sir, that this document does have Mr. Boban's signature, and let's confirm one thing, again. On the basis of the document we saw a moment ago, did you notice that Mr. Boban is mentioning funds for assistance to Croatia? They are documents from April 1992. Here, he says: "In recent times, there are more and more actions of gathering aid for Bosnia and Herzegovina, both in the Republic of Croatia and abroad. At this moment, that aid is of exceptional -- extreme importance." Then, he goes on to say that: "All your assistance for Bosnia-Herzegovina," I'd like to emphasise that, "Bosnia and Herzegovina, goes through Zagreb and our fund for aid to Croatia at Villach, Austria, which has been in existence for a long time, and is under the control of the government of the Republic of Croatia, which you used so far to make payments. Then it says: "On the payment orders, you can underline or transfer orders. You can underline that your contributions are intended for Bosnia and Herzegovina." Right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Boban goes on to say, in the second sentence of the penultimate paragraph, he says that: "Defence is not something that is specifically linked to just one village or municipality. That it is a question of the defence of Croatia and Bosnia-Herzegovina and the Croatian people as a whole, and that is why our defence must be comprehensive, complete," and then he goes on to say, "defence from the Chetnik hoards." And then we have these bank accounts; right? We have bank accounts into which the money was supposed to be paid. Now, clearly, from this document, it emerges that it is assistance and aid to both Croatia and Bosnia-Herzegovina; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now I'd like us to look -- well, Judge Antonetti asked you whether this was acted upon, but let's look at 2D 00543, one of my own documents. Tell me when you find it.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've found it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: This is a document from an Austrian bank. We can see, on the first page of the document, that this has to do with depositing funds in a particular account, 53.000 deutschemark. Mr. Jure Zovko made the payment, and we see on the right-hand side that the payment was made on the 27th of April, 1992. Sir, one thing that is very important: We see here the number of the account, and we see the name of the account. Could you please have a look at the previous document as well, that is to say, Mr. Boban's document, so that we are assured that this payment made is based on the previous document. We see the number, /647/643, and it says, "Funds for supporting Croatia, Bosnia-Herzegovina. Can we see that from the original? It can be seen in the translation, but we can see it in the original, too. I am going to give you time. It is of particular importance for me to -- for you to compare the numbers of these two accounts in this document and in Mr. Boban's proclamation.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first account in Mr. Boban's proclamation corresponds to the number here, and it has to do with German marks.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Sir, Mr. Jure Zovko made this payment; right? Is that is what is said here?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: We also have attached here a list of persons from whom this month any was collected. Mr. Zovko is number 3; am I right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: On the basis of these documents and your own knowledge from that period, the major donations were coming in for assistance to Bosnia-Herzegovina and the Croatian people in Bosnia-Herzegovina, and this money was actually paid abroad and arrived in the way that we just described and showed?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I have only two more groups of questions. One could be a bit longer, but could I --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me, counsel. Just before we leave that document, can I, so the record is clear, I take it it's the position of the Stojic Defence at least that then the Boban letter predates, predates April 1992. Is that your understanding, since you say the payments from the other document flow from that letter? So I take this letter is dated sometime prior to April 1992?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, my learned friend. As for this payment, document 2D 00543, you can see that the document is the 27th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On that document, you can see that the payment was made to the account that is referred to in Mr. Boban's document. That is document 2D 00532. The Defence is just claiming what is logical. May I just finish, please? We are saying the only logical thing; namely, that this document written by Mr. Boban must have been written before the 27th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In all fairness, in all fairness, this document does say that these funds for Bosnia-Herzegovina and Croatia were paid earlier; but in Mr. Boban's document, it says that: "In the future, this money should not be paid only for Croatia but also for Bosnia and Herzegovina," and that is shown by this document.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could counsel please speak up. We can barely hear her.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, counsel. So that the record is clear, then, the Boban letter is dated prior to April 27, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Stojic Defence did not say that. I just linked up two documents, and I drew a conclusion on the basis of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, what's your conclusion? I'm sorry to belabour the point, Your Honour, but I think it's a point worth making given what's been said by the Defence. Counsel, on one hand, I quite properly understood her to be saying, that she connected the two documents together, referred to the accounts, and specifically suggested that the contributions made on the -- as reflected in the document dated the 27th of April, 1992, flowed from Mr. Boban's letter, which is number 2D 00532. That's my understanding of it, and, therefore, counsel says it's only logical. I don't think it was a response. I don't think the month was coming in response to a letter that was sent sometime later. You can't respond to a letter that doesn't exist yet. I just asked counsel, and I thought it was fairly straightforward, if we could just have a confirmation, then, that Mr. Boban's letter is dated sometime prior to 27 April, 1992. It seems logical.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My learned friend, thank you, but it seems to me that you're trying to confuse me. I am not making a statement here. I am showing documents here, and I'm saying what my conclusions are on the basis of these documents. It is also the right of the Prosecution to draw their own conclusions on the basis of the documents that are here -- shown here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So the fact of the matter then is we don't know if there is any connection between the two. Counsel doesn't want to make the connection between the two documents then.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could you please cut this short --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- let's look at these three documents: There is Boban's letter, 20th of April, 1992, asking Soljic, Milolaza, Zrno to act when it comes to the payment of funds. This is document number one. The second document, this is the Nuremberg bank, 27th of April, 1992, with 53.000 deutschemark. There is a third document which is not dated, which was a letter which was probably sent by Boban to donors, which is undated, in which there is an account number, 350647643, for payments in deutschemark. The payment should be, no doubt, in a bank located in Austria. Nuremberg, for all those who are not aware of that, is not located in Austria. You can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] By your leave, I would just like briefly to say something in relation to a sentence from document 2D 00532. It is the second paragraph where Mr. Boban says: "All your assistance for Bosnia-Herzegovina goes through Zagreb, and our fund for supporting Croatia in Villach, Austria, which has been in existence for a long time now and which has been under the control of the government of Croatia and to which you have been making statements so far." And the most important sentence: "On the money orders, you can underline the assistance is meant for Bosnia and Herzegovina," and that is why I showed this document from the Austrian bank, where it does say that it is the fund for Croatia and Bosnia-Herzegovina. That is why I concluded that this proclamation written by Mr. Boban had to pre-date there money order.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You were a member of the HVO; and, later on, you started working in the Federal Ministry of Defence, as you explained to us; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can you tell me, as a member of the HVO and as a member of the Croatian component in the army of the federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina, you received vouchers for privatisation just like members of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: When was it that these privatisation vouchers were being handed out and when could you use these benefits? Tell me roughly what year this was?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 1999, 2000, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Did you get them precisely as a soldier of the HVO, and did these -- were these vouchers based on your total number of years of service in the HVO?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Let us explain this to the Court, if you can help me. Every member of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the HVO in Bosnia-Herzegovina received certain vouchers with which he could take part in the privatisation process of state property, and the value of these vouchers was established in accordance with the number of years of service spent in the HVO and the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina equally.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. 400 marks per month.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Perhaps the questions are going to seem too simple for you, but please answer them?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will proceed in a few minutes' time. We will have a 20-minute break now and resume afterwards. So we will have a 20-minute break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, as far as our timing is concerned, Ms. Nozica, you should have approximately 40 minutes left. Mr. Coric's Defence counsel has 15 minutes. Mr. Scott, how much time would you need for your redirect?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Obviously, Your Honour, I can only give an estimate since there's still outstanding cross-examinations, but I would expect perhaps around 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right. Mr. Coric's Defence counsel?

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wanted to say that we won't be having any questions, so we cede our 15 minutes to Ms. Nozica if she needs the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So, Ms. Nozica, if you would like to have these extra 15 minutes, this means that you have an hour.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I am almost certain that I'll be able to complete my cross-examination within 15 minutes. So with the time that Mr. Scott said he would need, this means that we ought to finish by the end of the day today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Well, if I'm at least in part responsible for that miracle to happen, then I'll be very happy.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Before the break, we talked about vouchers and privatisation, and you said that you had the same rights and the same rights were recognised through those vouchers your entire affiliation with the HVO; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Did every soldier in Siroki Brijeg have the same rights as HVO soldiers in Travnik, Sarajevo, Tuzla, Posavina, and Bihac?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So that means the same rights amongst themselves equal to all those rights that each member of the BH army had; right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I specified the rights to privatisation. Now, can you confirm that they also had all the other rights, the rights to a pension, the rights to receiving commendations, medals, and all the other rights that belonged to them while they were members of the HVO, that they were the same as members of the BH army members to the present day? They enjoy all those rights to today; right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. They have absolutely the same rights.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: The parliament of the federation, for example, of the federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina, decides about medals and commendations. Now, did the HVO members also have the right to receive medals and commendations for their participation in the HVO?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The members of the HVO had their commendations. They were not called the same as those for the -- the BH army, but they enjoyed the same rights. That is quite true.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, the HVO or members of the HVO, did they have the same status in all respects as the BH army members, if the members were a Croat, for example, and the command of the army of the federation was a Muslim and vice versa?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can you confirm that after the signature of the Washington Agreement, the Ministry of Defence of the federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina mostly functioned in such a way as if the minister was a Croat, the deputy was a Muslim, and vice versa? Is that how things worked?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: But, ultimately, all the rights for the members of both armies were equally recognised and they were treated equally; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, sir, I'd like to ask you, and this will be my final question, whether you know about this and can confirm it: For 1992 and 1993, the defence department did not compile its budget?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it did not compile its budget, for the simple reason that there were no indices on the basis of which you could calculate a budget.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So can that also be said for the civilian part of the HVO, as you call it? Do you know about that? Did they not calculate their budget for 1992 and 1993 for the same reasons?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They certainly didn't, because they weren't able to calculate it and compile it because we had no indicators according to which that could be done. You have to have certain parameters on the basis of which you're going to write it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. That completes my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, just before giving the floor to Mr. Scott for his redirect, I have a short question to put to you. I would like you to look at 2D 00150. As far as the HVO is concerned and the breakdown, how many Croatian, how many Muslim members make it up. Do you have this chart?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This chart, for the transcript, indicates that the total number of soldiers is 36.797, broken down as follows: 30.841 Croatians and 5.956 Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This chart provides a breakdown according to each brigade, and we can see that there are brigades which have a greater number of Muslim members. For instance, under point 5, 101st Brigade, there would be 35 per cent, 56 per cent, 34 per cent; 105th brigade would have where the Muslims are in the majority, 48.41; however, in some brigades, the 4th Brigade, for instance, out of 3.953, there are only 200 Muslims. I find these figures surprising. This clearly indicates that there are a great number of Muslims in the HVO. Were you aware of such a breakdown?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew that there were Bosniaks, that is to say, Muslims, in HVO units. Now, how many exactly, well, I didn't deal with that kind of thing. Quite simply, when calculating the active-duty salaries, I would come across Bosniak names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, having have a look at number 36, the Battalion of Convicts. Have you heard of this battalion?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question. Could you repeat it, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please look at point 36, item 36, the Convicts Battalion. They would be 280 in all. It seems that 116 members are Muslims, approximately 41 per cent. Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew there were Bosniaks, Muslims, in that unit. But how many exactly, I didn't know. Well, quite simply, I wasn't interested in that kind of thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. As this document was adduced by the Defence, I wanted to understand a few mention about it. Mr. Scott, you have the floor. You have plenty of time as we have 40 minutes left.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, and Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Scott, to avoid any difficulty, generally speaking, when we have redirect, this creates extra tension in the courtroom. When we talk about redirect, you must state that the Defence as put such-and-such the question, the witness has answered, and then you take it from there. The redirect should always be directly connected to the questions put by the Defence teams.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I think all the questions I put that I anticipate putting will be fairly -- it will be very clear that they flow from the Defence questions and Defence exhibits.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Just a couple of beginning points, Mr. Rupcic, and good afternoon. Can you just tell us, in case if it comes up in the future, we'll know this, where were you located and what were you doing in the period October/November 1993?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in the same place, in Grude.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And what was your position or title at that time?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in the financial department --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- underneath Mr. Pero Majic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And I take it, we can understand throughout your testimony over the last couple of days or so, that you were obviously not only working in Grude, but I assume you also lived in the Grude area throughout that time?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For a short period of time, we lived in the hotel at Grude; and when we had some free time, we could spend the night there; but Ljubuski is not a long way from Grude, and then I would go back and forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: But we can understand, then, that in October/November 1993, you were living and working in the Grude area; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not living; working, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And living in Ljubuski?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. I think I asked you about this, sir, but there's a second part that I'm not sure. I believe you've testified in the last couple of days that the amount of the HVO outstanding debt at the end of the war, I believe you told us the other day, was approximately 100.000.000 deutschemarks; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And I think I showed you some documents in relation to that. I don't recall if I asked you, but can you tell the Judges, as of approximately 2005, when you were -- when I spoke with you before, approximately how much of that debt, that 100.000.000 deutschemark debt, was still outstanding at that time?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I don't mind this, the question, but it isn't redirect. I just want to make sure that the Trial Chamber understands that, and especially, you know, if he can -- I don't see where he's going, how it's tied into the cross-examination. But this is not redirect, and this information was elicited on direct examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, if it was, if it was, and I agree that I have not researched the transcript for every entry, if the Chamber would humour me on this one question, I would appreciate it, if there's really an objection to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, can you recall -- can you remind us again, please, how much had been paid by 2005 out of this had 100.000.000 deutschemark debt, approximately?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: By 2005. Well, I can't tell you up until 2005. All I can tell you is up until the time I left the Ministry of Defence what it was, and it was the 1st of January, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And what was it?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 80.000.000 marks --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Outstanding?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- was the debt outstanding. Yes, outstanding. That was just the HVO component's debt. The Bosniak component was far greater.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. I would like to ask that you turn in the -- you still have the various bundles. You can take the bundle from the Prlic Defence team, please. Sir, I didn't want to interrupt you any more than I did during the cross-examinations, but I with like to explore your knowledge of some of these documents, and if you could please find, first of all, 1D 01771, 1D 01771.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So, just so we can be clear on this, you have no real personal knowledge of this decision or anything that happen at any meeting where this decision was taken, do you?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And if you could look at Exhibit 1D 01760 --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If I just might register an observation, Your Honour. Again, I have no objection to the Prosecution doing this. This is a technique that I picked up from the Prosecution. They've been doing it for the last 18 months, and I find that what's good for the Prosecution is good for the Defence. So I don't mind wasting the next 20 minutes, if that what he intends to do, but might I remind the Trial Chamber that routinely they bring in witnesses here. They show them documents which they've never ever seen, and then they elicit testimony from; and yet -- and then documents, they then introduce by way of motion, hundreds, in the thousands of pages of which there is absolutely no viva voce testimony. The whole purpose of the cross-examination was not whether the gentleman attended these sessions. Now, if the gentleman from the Prosecution office wishes to contest the authenticity of these documents, and I dare say he should not because he can find them in the Official Gazettes that are available and were available to him throughout the seven years that he's been working on this case, that's a different matter. But the content is what it is, and I don't see the point in this exercise. But if we do go down this road, I certainly would want the Defence to be availed of the very same process.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. Karnavas has just said he doesn't really have an objection, so this is commentary and I don't want to waste my time responding to a non-objection. So if we could please go to 1D 01760.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: This was a document that Mr. Karnavas showed you by Mr. Topic and asked you about the intention or the design of indicating that transitions should take place in Croatian or Yugoslav dinars. Sir, you can't tell these Judges what Mr. Topic's intentions were, can you? Did you talk to Mr. Tomic about this decision and what his goal was in adopting this decision?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Objection. There was no mentioning of Mr. Tomic. Mr. Tomic has nothing to do with this, unless he can connect this. But you this is Topic, not Tomic. They are two different individuals and one has one to do with the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. Topic, sir. Mr. Topic, sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
