utterances.text: The Mostar municipality, in its session of the 25th of July, 1992, passed the following decision, were you present at this session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said Topic, not Tocic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, this document refers to this decision having been taken at the session of the July 25th, 1992 meeting of the Mostar municipality. Were you present at that session?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did you talk to any people who were present at that meeting who explained to you what their intentions were in adopting that decision?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, I wasn't present, nor did I talk to anybody, any of the people who were there at the meeting, but I did know why the Jugo dinar was being banned from the territory, because there was a general looting going on after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: The Jugo dinar. Okay. Could you go please to 1D 01762, 1D 01762. There's a reference in the heading under the words "Decision." It talks about the professionalisation of the army, and I think two Defence counsel showed you this document. It talks about the adequate salaries of TIP. Can you tell us what "TIP" stands for?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that this is a mistake, and that's my personal opinion now. It's a typing mistake because TIP, T-I-P, is not actually an abbreviation. It was a professional army of the type, T-Y-P-E, type 1 and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Just so the record is clear, when you say there's a mistake, we're not just referring to the English transcript, but that's the way it's written. It's also T-I-P in the Croatian-language version, which I assume is the one you were looking at. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Read it in your own language. Read paragraph II in your own language so that the interpreters can translate it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it says the right thing: "The decision on professionalising the army within the Petar Kresimir IV brigade of the HVO and determining adequate salaries of the type A. So when we discussing whether you or I, or whatever the discussion was that we had here, I said that a professional soldier at a certain period of time had a salary of about 400 deutschemarks when the inflation was rampant. So this would drop to 200 and then go to 400. And the active-duty had about 150 to 200 German marks. That's was what their salary was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And when it makes reference to in the second numbered paragraph, II; the special salary, do you know what "the special salary" was?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I've just explained to you. That's the type A salary for professional soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And do you know whether this was a supplementation that was being given at this time to the HVO salaries or how much was coming from the Livno municipal HVO?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is something that the Livno municipality paid out.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I know that, sir, but were they paying the entire salary, are you suggesting, of this unit, or was it a supplemental payment, or was it a one-time payment, or what can you actually tell us about what's the content of this document?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's like this: What I can read from this document is this: I don't know if I can remember all the details. Members of the active-duty units, or rather, this unit, the active soldiers received salaries from Grude, but only the active-duty personnel with the commanders as specified in the establishment booklet, and all the reserve units were paid by the Livno municipality. Now, by some decision of theirs, that is to say, the Livno municipality, for reasons known to them alone, asked that their unit be, if I can put it this way, professionalised, or rather, that they would be paid the same amount as the professional soldiers of the HVO received.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Can I ask you to go to P -- excuse me, I'm sorry, 1D 00858. 1D 00858.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you share with us any knowledge you have about how this platoon was organised and financed?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It refers to a unit which belonged to the BH army, so I can't really tell you anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And what can you tell us about this reward? In II, it says: "Pursuant to the unit commander's assessment, this reward can be granted to the whole unit ..." What did you know about this reward?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It refers to the BH army. As I just said, I wasn't a member of the BH army, so you can't expect me to interpret that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. So you don't really know anything about the document. Can I ask you to go to 2D 00538. 538, my apology -- no, I guess I was right, 38.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's just in the other binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sorry. It's in there, yes. Thank you. If you can just scan down this page or this document, please, I think it was presented to you, if I'm not mistaken, as related to the HVO military, and perhaps you can just confirm that there's nothing in this document that indicates that it relates to the HVO military, but is financing for the HVO municipal organisation.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, that was the document that I presented to the witness, and I didn't say that it referred to the financing of the military sector but of the HVO municipality of the Livno municipality, and I didn't bring that into connection with the military wing. I was discussing the municipality's defence, the defence of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: The witness has answered, Your Honour, and the transcript will certainly speak for itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, you indicated again, in response to a question of counsel for Mr. Stojic, that, again, it was Mr. Boban making all the financial decisions of the military arm of Herceg-Bosna. Can you just describe to us how Mr. Boban would go about making those decisions?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Your Honour. Your Honour, I do apologise, but the witness never ever said that Mr. Boban made all the decisions. I asked the witness whether, because of a lack of resources in 1993 and 1992, certain decisions on the redistribution of funds were made by Mr. Boban. Now, if the Prosecutor shows me where the witness said that, I must say that I didn't note that because that wasn't my intention at all.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I talked to you and here in court, I also said that I was never present when Mr. Boban made any decisions. However, Mr. Majic sat in the same office as me across from me; and, so, from what he told me, I can confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And how did Mr. Boban go about making these decisions? What information did he consider? Who did he talk to first? What documents did he have in front of him? Perhaps you can help us with that.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't there. I didn't attend the meetings. I wasn't present. I would happen to meet people in the corridor, and we would communicate that way, people coming to see Mr. Boban. I knew some of these people from earlier on in our civilian life. And, so, after they would go into his office, Mr. Boban's office, Mr. Majic would be called to attend; and when he returned, he would make out payments, money orders, or whatever.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: But you answered the first part of my question, and that is you don't know who he talked to. You don't know how decisions were made; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, as I said, how did Mr. Boban go about making these decisions in his office? Who did he consult with? What documents did he have in front of them? Please, tell us.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I assure the Court that I am quite serious about these questions. There is no humour involved in this at all. He made certain decisions, and I want to know the basis for those being given.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Tell us, please. How many times did he receive faxes from the HVO Main Staff? How many telephone calls did he make?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're asking me something now. Well, how would you expect me to know that?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Exactly, sir. You don't know, do you?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. I don't, and I never said I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If you can please look at Exhibit P 08118, it's the annual report of the ONP that we looked at several times, including on cross-examination. In reference, if you can find the page that we were looking at, Mr. Stojic's counsel was asking you about the numbers. It's the first real page of columns of numbers, and we were talking about the money coming from the Republic of Croatia, for example. Do you have that? What "Revenue from Budget"?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Under "Revenue from budget and donations," apart the Ministry of Defence portion, do you see under that "the HZ HB finance department Mostar"?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Do you know -- and then it indicates 131.000.000.000 dinar. Can you tell the Chamber how that 131 -- what that 131.000.000.000 dinar, how that's comprised? Where did that money come from?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, as I've already told you, the funds were collected from taxes and contributions and customs dues and donations paid into that particular account; that is to say, the resident account in Opuzen.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So you're saying that 131.000.000.00 dinar, we should be able to find that, you're saying, in the account at Privredna Banka that we looked at?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on the cards that we were looking at earlier on from Privredna Banka, the commercial bank, and the financial department; that is to say, the civilian part. We looked at expenditures and revenues.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: My apology. I cut off the interpretation. In the portion, that's titled "Received in deutschemarks." And about the seventh -- perhaps the seventh item down, once again is the finance department Mostar, we see again 16.790.000.000, et cetera, which I think everyone can see accounts for the very vast majority of everything in the bottom number of 19 billion. Again, can you tell us where that 16.790.000.000 came from?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What figure are you referring to can you repeat that please?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Next to the finance department Mostar, 16.790.935.555.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here: Finance department, 131.000.000 million. As for the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Croatia, they provided 16.000.000.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I think we must be looking at a different document, sir. Finance department Mostar, you're looking at German marks. First item is Republic of Croatia Ministry of Defence; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Then we go down one, two, three, four, five lines down. Do you see "HR HB finance department"?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Do you see the number 16.000.000.000?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. My question to you was: Do you know where that money came from?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean where they came from? They came from the foreign currency account of the civilian finance department.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And how do you -- well, do you really know the breakdown at all? Do you really know where that money came from? Do you have personal knowledge of the sources and amounts of money that make up that 16.000.000.000 dinar?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. I wouldn't know that. Off-the-cuff, I would have to look into documents and establish everything. But if you turn it into German marks, the amount would be 4.000.000 German marks.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm not arguing with your math, although I certainly haven't done it as quickly as you have. But the answer is: You don't know. You really don't know what that money consists of specifically. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. German mark and Croatian dinar was the currency that was used and depended on the person providing the funds whether they would make the payment in German marks or in Croatian dinars.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Rupcic. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, if you turn to the English version of this document, this is the annual report financial statement, on page 7. I don't know whether you can answer my question. But as far as item "Receipt in German marks" is concerned, I see "Received in German marks. Republic of Croatia, Ministry of Defence, Zagreb." If I understood you correctly, this was money sent by private individuals, donors, that transited through the Ministry of Defence in Zagreb; is that correct? Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, then, second item: Croatian Catholic mission, Esslingen. What is this about? Is this also private donors or the church, the parish?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that town in Esslingen, there is a Catholic -- Croatian Catholic mission, and members, parishioners of that mission raised the funds and made the payment into a savings account, from which the money was then taken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. If I've understood you correctly, these are private individuals who provide the funds, and it is not the parish or the religious authority in that location. I didn't understand your answer.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You have to realise that Catholic missions throughout the world joined into fundraising efforts for the defence -- defensive war. This was true in Australia, in America, in Germany, and anywhere in the world where Catholic missions exist. Croatia is a Catholic country. Bosnia and Herzegovina -- or rather, in Bosnia and Herzegovina, one of the constituent people are Catholics by religion, and they raised funds for the defence of Catholic people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't understand. We're talking about private individuals X, Y, Z, who privately decided to collect the money, whether it be the archbishop or the parish priest who collects the funds and then hands them over.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The person who headed the Catholic mission was somebody they trusted, then members of that mission brought the money to him, and then he in turn would -- just as we saw in another example. There was another document showing 50.000 deutschemarks were raised, and next to that was a list specifying who gave exactly how much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm sorry. I do have one question, just a clarification, and I do admit it's just to clarify a number. I just simply wanted -- if the Chamber doesn't want the witness to give an answer, I'll certainly accept that. I simply wanted to clarify, on page 8, "the Republic of Croatia Ministry of Defence Zagreb," the reference to "911.750." I simply wanted to ask the witness if he could clarify what form of -- unit of currency it was. I don't know at that point of the chart whether we're still walking about dinars, dollars, deutschemarks. If I could please clarify that, if I'm allowed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, please do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Towards the end of the statement of revenue, several lines up from the bottom, there is another reference to Republic of Croatian Ministry of Defence Zagreb. Can you help us with what the units of currency were?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, can you add up apples and pears, or apples and oranges? It says herein the amount is in Swiss franks. Maybe it was in Swiss franks initially, but then later on all the amounts were converted into Croatian dinar. So all the amounts in this report are in Croatian dinar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You mean except where they say specifically say German deutschemarks or American dollars or Swiss franks or Austrian shillings.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV RUPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are converted as well, sir. This is not a case where 268.000.000 marks was withdrawn but, rather, 268.000.000 Croatian dinars. When you convert it, you see that it's about 60.000 marks.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, for counsel.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. If I may intervene to assist. Would you please look at the top of this list. I think that would clarify Mr. Scott's question. It says here: "The structure of revenue from the 1st of January, 1993 until the 31st of December expressed in Croatian dinars, but received in different currencies." This is what the witness is saying, and this is what the document reflects as well. All the amounts in the document are expressed in Croatian dinar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it looks quite clear. In the chart we have in front us, everything is denominated in Croatian dinars, but some amounts have been paid in foreign currency. The Catholic parish of Lausanne has paid the money in Swiss franks, but the Swiss franks have been converted to Croatian dinars. Is that right, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct, Your Honour. In bookkeeping, there are synthetic accounts and analytical accounts. In synthetic accounts, you have an amount of 185 billion and some millions. That's synthetic account, and it reflects revenue. And, in analytical accounts, you can see the breakdown, where it actually says, Miro raised and provided this much, and Pero provided this much. I'm now simplifying it. But in the analytical account, you can see the breakdown. You can see exactly what the revenue was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. President. I was simply trying to be very clear about some numbers at the end of the document. I'm sorry if I'm the own one who may have had some confusion. I apologise, but I thank the witness for the answer. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Witness, on behalf of my colleagues, I'd like to thank you for having come to testify on the request of the Prosecution. I wish you a safe journey home. You have raised your hand. What would you like to say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I didn't come here at the invitation of the Prosecution. I came pursuant to the order of the Chamber. I was subpoenaed here, and this is how I came to be here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. That goes without saying, but, initially, the Prosecutor had asked you to come. It wasn't the Defence, and it wasn't the Trial Chamber either. So I wish you a safe journey home, and I wish you well in the future also. It is somewhat uncertain, given your past history, but you should be able to start on a new journey in your professional -- in a professional environment soon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So as far as next week is concerned. Mr. Scott how are things going to unfold next week?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: We have one witness which will again take up the week, or at least some part of it. As we see today, it might -- you know, we may finish by Wednesday if we don't go into Thursday day, but we are arranged. We do have a witness arranged. I do have one other matter, Your Honour, again, just in terms of all the outstanding paperwork. Earlier this week, Your Honour, responses were filed by the Defence to the Heliodrom 92 bis motion and also to an earlier motion concerning approximately, I don't have the exact number in my mind, but approximately 300 documents. We, the Prosecution, would like to have and ask to have until the 22nd of October to reply.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Karnavas, did you get up to discuss this or something else?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No. If it were up to me, I would grant the request.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So your wishes have come true because the Trial Chamber grants you until the 22nd of October, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Just very quickly, Your Honours. There was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very quickly, because we've overstepped our time. Please quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: On the 27th of September, 2007, in the Prosecutor versus Perisic case, there was a decision that came down regarding the Defence's request for -- for a B/C/S transcript of the accused's statement in that case. Judge Robinson ordered that the Prosecution provide a B/C/S version of the transcript given that the Prosecution in that case, as in this case, is attempting to use that -- that interview as part of their case. I would, at this point in time, I'm making an oral application for an order to the Prosecution to transcribe the -- the interview, given that as it was stated by Judge Robinson that -- that this is an obligation that the Prosecution cannot be relieved of, especially given the magnitude and importance of the -- of what is at stake. The accused is entitled to have this sort of document in his or her own language. So I ask for an order. You know, I don't need it right now, but at some point I wish for the Trial Bench to order the Prosecution to commence with the translation of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I am discovering this. Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Two brief responses, Your Honours. Of course, the Chamber should be aware that this was a videotaped, this was a videotaped interview, and a full set of the videotapes were not only given to the Defence in connection with disclosure in this case, but were given to Mr. Prlic back at the original date when the statement was taken. So all the -- all the questions and answers in Croatian or B/C/S, whichever term one wants to use, are available to -- to Mr. Prlic in his own language; in fact, his own words. You can hear his own words on the videotape, and we have provided that a long time ago. I think a number of Chambers - I didn't anticipate this question being raised by Mr. Karnavas. I'm not complaining - but I believe it's been a long-standing practice in a number of Chambers that the provision of a recording satisfies the requirement to provide it in a language the accused understands. Number one. Number two, Your Honour, if the Chamber wants a hard copy B/C/S translation to be prepared, we can certainly refer that to CLSS. I have no idea when they will be able to get to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. President, in the Perisic case, it was videotapes. I am sure Mr. Scott knows or should have known about it. That's number one. And number two, it's quite clear the obligations of -- of the Prosecution concerning this sort of -- this sort of matter. Now, we have made a request. The registry pointed us to this -- to this decision and asked that the Trial Chamber issue an order, and so we are asking for an order. We're asking that this be done by December, by December 13th. And if the Prosecution has to hire outside sources to do it, they should do it. They have a war chest, a war chest.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I hope this is helpful. In the Krajisnik case, it isn't a translation that is required. It is just a transcription. So the task is less actually less daunting, and, therefore, there is all the more reason why Mr. Karnavas's application should be granted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. As the Chamber will meet in a few minutes' time, we will deliberate and let you know what decision we take. We shall adjourn and meet again on Monday at a quarter past 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 15th day of October, 2007, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.50 p.m.,
